key_insight: MonarchRT shows that by redesigning attention for the few-step, autoregressive diffusion setting, you can avoid the failure modes of prior sparse approximations and retain high-quality video generation while sharply reducing attention cost and latency.
problem_solved: Addresses the quadratic cost and brittleness of 3D self-attention in real-time, few-step autoregressive video diffusion where errors compound across frames and denoising steps.
method: Reformulate spatio-temporal attention to prioritize information that must be preserved across few-step, autoregressive denoising (e.g., compress global context, strengthen temporally-critical keys).
Combine lightweight local spatial attention with an efficient global/temporal routing or memory mechanism so cross-frame coherence is preserved without full 3D quadratic attention.
Design attention primitives and routing heuristics that are robust to compounding errors typical of few-step autoregressive diffusion, enabling faster denoising with minimal quality loss.
impact: Enables practical real-time video diffusion by reducing latency and compute while maintaining generation fidelity in low-step, autoregressive regimes — useful for live applications, edge deployment, and interactive content creation.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing replacement of full 3D self-attention with MonarchRT's hybrid attention (local spatial + compressed global/temporal routing).
Latency vs. quality plot comparing full 3D attention, prior sparse approximations, and MonarchRT in few-step autoregressive generation.
Sequence visualization illustrating how MonarchRT preserves frame-to-frame coherence and prevents error accumulation across denoising steps.
Icon set showing benefits: lower compute (chip icon), lower latency (stopwatch), maintained quality (film/frame icon).
paper_title: MonarchRT: Efficient Attention for Real-Time Video Generation
paper_authors: Krish Agarwal, Zhuoming Chen, Cheng Luo, Yongqi Chen, Haizhong Zheng
